Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S2-01] Plan the chapter's videos from the chapter map: first one short 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video (5-8 minutes) that teaches the chapter's prerequisites, then the topic videos in teaching order. Narration is 6-8 minutes per book page (Navin, 23 October 2026; the 14-page tissue chapter about 85-110 minutes of topic videos, plus the prerequisite video): each topic video gets the share of the pages its items come from, and a very dense page may go up to 25% over when the plan says why. Understanding (Section 1) and the chapter map have no time limit.
[S2-02] Write a spoken teacher script in beats with a natural teacher flow. Stories and analogies only where they genuinely help that topic. Every item the book teaches is taught and every teacher question answered from the book is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the time allows. Cut repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S2-03] Prerequisites are only what this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite. They are taught, not named, in the chapter's 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video, each with a simple explanation and an example; a topic video may remind of them in at most 2 beats.
[S2-04] Spoken Hinglish the way Navin teaches, in mixed script (Navin, 21 and 23 October 2026): Hindi words in Devanagari, English words, above all the book's technical terms, in Roman exactly as the book spells them, as in 'आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे'; a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical; not in BIE's everyday word list rulebook/simple_hindi.json) gets its English word in brackets right after it, as in 'सतह (surface)'; the screen and subtitles show the bracket and the voice says 'सतह, यानी surface'. Never a bracket after an everyday word or inside an idiom or a fixed phrase ('आम तौर पर', not 'आम तौर (usually) पर'; 'नहीं के बराबर', not 'नहीं के बराबर (equal to)'). Never an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman. Numbers as digits; short spoken sentences addressed to one student; questions to the student and natural pauses; no reading out of lists.
[S2-05] Every beat states which chapter-map items it covers and which teacher questions it answers, and those claims must be true: the beat really explains that item and really answers that question.
[S2-06] Teach every part of a video through the universal frame (what the process is, how it works, when and in what order, under which conditions, in what atmosphere) and through the teaching pattern of its content type, step by step in the pattern's order; every item on the task card is really taught, none only named.
[S2-07] Open every book line in the script, never read it out (Navin, 24 October 2026). A new topic opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any book line the beat carries at least one of: the term's plain meaning with 'yaani' and an everyday image, a why step from a need, an example or the place. Speak complete sentences, not clipped notes. A classification is taught as a family: the overview tree, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence), then the members compared and a memory trick. A pattern step may be skipped only with a stated reason; one recap per part and one closing recap.
[S2-08] Apply first, name after (Navin, 27 October 2026): in an economics script a concept's real-world example runs BEFORE the beat that names the term: the example beats carry the example's numbers (₹50 → ₹65, buyers 2 → 12 → 3) and walk the mechanism step by step; then the term ('isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain'), then the book's definition, then one line on where the learner meets it in real life. The example is the one Section 1 chose for the item (its place, actors, goods, numbers), economically correct and at the learner's level.
[W-01] The narration never points at the book: no 'book के अनुसार', 'किताब कहती है', 'book says', 'page पर', 'textbook', 'NCERT' or any wording of that family (the list in this file, 'wording'). BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a write_script card:
- card.parts are this video's parts: each has item ids, one content type and the questions it must answer. The source gives every item's
  full content and its teacher questions with ids ("p003-i4#q2") and answers from BIE's chapter map; teach from them.
- card.coverage.must_cover lists every item this video must teach: each must be in covers_item_ids of a beat that really explains it.
  may_skip lists items you may leave out (not teachable). card.context.map_slice shows the related concepts for context only.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what this video is about, the key questions it must answer, your main decisions (order,
  hook, analogy, where prerequisites are taught) with a reason each, what is uncertain.
- title: the video title in the learner language.
- parts: one entry per card part, with the universal frame of that part (S3-01), each in one or two lines of clear English for BIE:
  process (what happens or what the thing does), how (how it works or happens), when (when, in what order, under which timing),
  conditions (what must be true for it, or what changes it), atmosphere (the setting and situation a student should picture). Write
  "n/a: " and the reason only where a question truly does not apply to that part. skipped_steps = the teaching-pattern steps of this
  part you leave out because there is nothing real to say for them, each with the reason ([] when every step is done); at most half
  of a pattern, never a step that has something real; BIE's code records the reason.
- beats: the whole video in order. beat_id "b1", "b2" ...; part_id = the card part this beat teaches ("" for the opening hook, a
  prerequisite taught first, a transition or the final recap); step = the number of the teaching-pattern step of that part's content type
  that this beat performs (see the content types above; 0 when part_id is "" and for an exam-question part, whose type is "none");
  the steps of a part's pattern appear in order, except the ones skipped with a reason; a classification part follows the family
  pattern: the overview tree first, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape → why it is named so → its special feature
  → its function with its cause → where it is found, by a zoom from the organ → its consequence), then the comparison, then a memory
  trick; one recap per part and one closing recap for the video, never two recaps of the same thing;
  purpose (hook, prerequisite, explain, example, analogy, story, compare, process_walkthrough, misconception, exam_tip,
  question_to_student, recap, transition); say = the exact spoken words, one to four complete spoken sentences in Navin's Hinglish
  (S2-04), the way a teacher speaks to one student, never clipped note-style lines ("Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular." is a teacher's
  beat; "Location: kidney tubules, glandular ducts." is a note):
  mixed script: Hindi words in Devanagari, English words (above all the book's technical terms, spelled as the book spells them) in
  Roman, as in "आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे"; brackets only after a genuinely difficult Hindi word (see "Brackets" below; the
  screen shows the bracket and the voice says "सतह, यानी surface"); never write an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman;
  numbers as digits; addressed to one student; covers_item_ids = the item ids this beat really explains; answers = the teacher question
  ids this beat really answers; on_screen = what the student should see while hearing it (for the director); basis = book, outside or
  mixed.
Opening the book (S2-07; BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher, never a reader of the line): every new
topic (every concept and every prerequisite) opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any
book line, the beat carries at least one of: the term opened ("yaani" + its plain meaning + one everyday image), the why from a need or
a problem, or an example or place by a zoom from the organ. The source gives every item's unpack from Section 1 (its terms, why chain,
example, consequence, visual verb) and the locked explanations: speak them, in your own teacher's words, at the depth of the level
profile below. BIE's code sends back a beat whose English words are the book's and that opens nothing ("dohraav pakad"), a clipped
sentence without a verb, a topic that opens without a question, and a second recap of the same thing.
Real-world application (S2-08; Navin, 27 October 2026: "economic concepts ko real world mein apply karke samjhao"): for an economics
definition, cause_effect or process item the source gives the real_world_example Section 1 chose (place, actors, goods, numbers before
→ after, the steps with their mechanism links, the naming sentence, the real-life link). Run that example FIRST, in beats that cover
the item and carry its numbers as digits ("dukaan mein chini ke 3 packet, ₹50 ka ek; kal 2 khareedar, aaj 12"), walking the mechanism
step by step (purpose story or example); only then the beat that names the term ("isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain"), then
the book's definition, then the real-life link. The opening question of such a topic asks about the situation, not the term. BIE's
code sends back a script whose naming beat comes before the example beats, or whose example beats carry none of the numbers.
Time (S2-01): the source gives this video's narration time; BIE's code counts the spoken words (130 a minute) and the script must stay
within it. Win the time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content: every item in must_cover is taught and every
teacher question whose basis is "book" is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the
time allows.
Prerequisites (S2-03): in a topic video they were already taught in the prerequisite video; remind of one in at most 2 beats (purpose
"prerequisite"). In the prerequisite video (card parts "pre1", "pre2" ...) teach each prerequisite simply, with an everyday example, in
the order given: part_id = the prerequisite id, step 0, covers_item_ids = the prerequisite ids the beat teaches, answers [].
A beat introduces at most a few new items: BIE's code measures the load of every beat (0.4 per new item plus 1 per 50 spoken words, at
most 1.8), so a beat holds at most about 70 spoken words with one new item, 50 with two and 30 with three; split longer beats. Reply
with the JSON object only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-27.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- Open with a question on something visible (every new topic and every new family member): Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Contrast with the neighbour (members of one family, and what the exam confuses): Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
- Ask and repeat the key word (the one word the learner must keep): Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular.
- Exam memory beats by level (after the understanding, by the level profile): Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.
- Apply it in the real world first, then name it (Navin's sugar shop) (every economics concept (a definition, a cause-and-effect chain, a process): the example runs before the term is named): Ek kirana shop mein chini ke 3 packet hain, ₹50 ka ek. Kal 2 khareedar aaye the, aaj 12 aa gaye; sab ko chini chahiye par packet 3 hi hain. Dukandar daam ₹65 kar deta hai; ab sirf 3 log kharid paate hain, baaki 9 khaali haath. Zyada log, utna hi maal, isliye daam upar. Isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain. Phir book ki definition. Phir: yahi aap Diwali se pehle sabzi mandi mein dekhte hain.

Brackets (word list 2026-10-27.1): use everyday spoken Hindi freely, without brackets (मुख्य, वापस, बराबर, आसपास, इस्तेमाल, करके, जिससे ...). Only a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical) gets its English word in brackets right after it, for example "सतह (surface)", "घर्षण (friction)", "सघन (dense)"; better still, use the book's English term or a simpler Hindi word. Never put a bracket inside an idiom or a fixed phrase: "आम तौर पर", not "आम तौर (usually) पर"; "नहीं के बराबर", not "नहीं के बराबर (equal to)". BIE's code removes a bracket after an everyday word and asks for one only after a Hindi word it does not know as everyday.

frame.process: Trace the gold–Dollar arrangement from 1944 to the termination of convertibility in 1971.
frame.how: Explain the original anchor, accumulating pressures and Nixon's decision.
frame.when: 1944, the 1960s and 15 August 1971, in that order.
frame.conditions: Confidence depends on the credibility of the official gold-conversion promise.
frame.atmosphere: International trade needs usable balances while official holders seek dependable backing.

frame.process: Explain the conversion rate and the Dollar's reserve-currency role.
frame.how: Build conversion arithmetic and distinguish reserve assets from payments using them.
frame.when: Under the historical gold-linked arrangement, before the 1971 break.
frame.conditions: Conversion applied mainly to foreign central banks; numerical transactions are hypothetical.
frame.atmosphere: French and US authorities settle gold claims and machinery payments through banks.

frame.process: Explain why increasing external Dollar claims strained confidence in gold redemption.
frame.how: Compare the gold needed for claims with available gold, then contrast liquidity with confidence.
frame.when: Pressures accumulated by the 1960s, before the 1971 decision.
frame.conditions: The conflict appears when external claims grow without sufficient growth in gold.
frame.atmosphere: Trade expands while official holders worry about the conversion promise.

frame.process: Read the gold–Dollar–other currencies hierarchy.
frame.how: Trace the three boxes and two arrows from top to bottom.
frame.when: Read as a relationship within the arrangement, not a chronology.
frame.conditions: Arrows indicate monetary links, not physical gold shipments or retail conversion rights.
frame.atmosphere: A three-level diagram connects a familiar Rupee to the international monetary anchor.

frame.process: Connect the 1973 oil shock with the 1974 Saudi–US understanding.
frame.how: Explain restricted supply, higher prices, Saudi financial commitments and US security commitments.
frame.when: 1973 precedes the 1974 understanding.
frame.conditions: Pricing and investment are separate commitments; illustrative allocations are not historical shares.
frame.atmosphere: Oil importers face expensive supplies while Saudi Arabia and the US exchange financial and security commitments.

frame.process: Explain continuing Dollar demand from oil-payment requirements.
frame.how: Follow an enlarged Dollar invoice through a bank into payment demand.
frame.when: After gold convertibility ends, whenever oil invoices require Dollars.
frame.conditions: Dollar pricing is neither oil redemption nor a guarantee of exchange-value stability.
frame.atmosphere: An Indian oil importer obtains foreign currency to pay a seller.

frame.process: Answer why Dollars could still be held without gold backing.
frame.how: Apply the distinction between redemption backing and transaction demand.
frame.when: After teaching the oil-payment channel.
frame.conditions: The invoice specifies Dollars even though gold conversion is unavailable.
frame.atmosphere: A conceptual exam question tests whether the learner confuses backing with usefulness.

beats.say: विदेश का bill चुकाने को Dollars चाहिए, लेकिन Dollars रखने वाले gold भी माँग लें, तो क्या होगा? आज यही तनाव समझेंगे, फिर देखेंगे कि gold का वादा खत्म होने पर भी Dollars क्यों चाहिए थे।
beats.on_screen: Trade-payment need versus gold-conversion confidence.

beats.say: अलग देशों के पैसे किस जोड़ से जुड़े थे? 1944 का Bretton Woods System gold, Dollar और दूसरी currencies को जोड़ता था; international payments के लिए भरोसे वाला ढाँचा चाहिए था।
beats.on_screen: 1944 → 1960s → 1971; gold → Dollar → currencies.

beats.say: मान लो eligible French monetary authority US$350 देकर gold माँगे, तो कितना मिलेगा? इस काल्पनिक official conversion में US$350 का दावा घटकर US$0 होगा और उसे 10 troy ounces gold मिलेगा।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: claims US$350 → US$0; gold received 0 → 10 troy ounces.

beats.say: यही fixed gold convertibility है: US का वादा था US$35 के बदले 1 troy ounce gold देना, मुख्यतः foreign central banks को। यह हर व्यक्ति की gold बदलने वाली सुविधा नहीं थी।
beats.on_screen: US$35 ↔ 1 troy ounce; mainly foreign central banks.

beats.say: अब machinery का US$350 bill कैसे चुकाएँगे? काल्पनिक French importer अपने bank को घरेलू रकम देता है; authority Dollars देती है और exporter को US$350 मिलता है। दूसरी inflow न हो तो official reserves US$700 से US$350 रहेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: importer → bank → US exporter; reserves US$700 → US$350.

beats.say: इस international उपयोग में Dollar world's reserve currency बना। यानी authorities विदेश के payments में काम आने वाले assets Dollar में रखती थीं, जैसे आगे का bill भरने के लिए रखा balance।
beats.on_screen: Reserve currency: internationally usable official assets.

beats.say: Troy ounce पैसे की नहीं, gold तौलने की unit है, लगभग 31.1 grams। इसलिए 10 troy ounces लगभग 311 grams होंगे, 10 coins नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 1 troy ounce ≈ 31.1 g; 10 ≈ 311 g.

beats.say: इस historical arrangement में rate US$35 था; Dollar की बीच वाली जगह और trade के लिए उसकी जरूरत, उसका reserve role समझाते हैं। हमारे French transactions केवल समझाने के उदाहरण हैं, historical आँकड़े नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Historical terms ≠ illustrative transaction amounts.

beats.say: तय gold मिलने का भरोसा रखने में मदद करता था, जबकि trade में उपयोग Dollars की जरूरत बनाता था। ध्यान रहे, reserve रखा हुआ stock है; payment उस stock से बाहर जाने वाला flow हो सकता है।
beats.on_screen: Gold promise → confidence; international payments → usefulness.

beats.say: Conversion का हिसाब रखो: Dollar claim को US$35 से भाग दो, तो troy ounces मिलेंगे। US$350 ÷ 35 = 10; official conversion और import payment अलग transactions हैं।
beats.on_screen: Gold in troy ounces = eligible Dollar claim ÷ 35.

beats.say: अगर दावे बढ़ें लेकिन gold न बढ़े तो? काल्पनिक US importer French machinery के US$350 देता है; banks से ये Dollars French authority तक पहुँचते हैं और उसके claims US$350 से US$700 हो जाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical external payment: French official claims US$350 → US$700.

beats.say: US gold 10 troy ounces ही रहे, तो US$700 बदलने को 20 चाहिए। US$350 बदलते ही 10 ounces खत्म, और US$350 दावा बाकी: बढ़ते external claims से conversion पर दबाव ऐसे पड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Gold available 10; required 20; after one conversion: gold 0, claim US$350.

beats.say: 1960s तक US ने Vietnam War और welfare programs पर भारी खर्च किया। दुनिया में फैले Dollars के मुकाबले conversion के लिए US gold कम पड़ रहा था; France gold माँगने लगा।
beats.on_screen: 1960s: heavy spending; growing external Dollars; French gold demands.

beats.say: Trade बढ़े तो payment buffer कितना चाहिए? काल्पनिक French जरूरत US$350 से US$700 हुई; US buyers के payments से अतिरिक्त US$350 मिले, लेकिन gold 10 ounces ही रहा और पूरे conversion की जरूरत 20 हो गई।
beats.on_screen: Desired buffer 350 → 700; holdings 350 → 700; gold 10 → 10; required 10 → 20.

beats.say: यही built-in contradiction economist Robert Triffin ने पहचाना; इसे Triffin dilemma भी कहते हैं। Trade को ज्यादा Dollars चाहिए, लेकिन ज्यादा claims से gold मिलने का भरोसा कमजोर होता है; Dollars रोकें तो payments की जरूरत अधूरी रहे।
beats.on_screen: More liquidity ↔ weaker conversion confidence.

beats.say: France का gold माँगना इसी कमजोर कड़ी को सामने लाया। एक demand ने पूरा तनाव बनाया नहीं; बढ़ते trade balances और सीमित gold के बीच तनाव पहले से था।
beats.on_screen: Gold demand exposes the structural tension.

beats.say: हर domestic खर्च अपने-आप foreign Dollar claim नहीं बनता; बीच में international payments चाहिए। और Dollars की गिनती को gold के वजन से सीधे नहीं, conversion rate लगाकर तुलना करेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Domestic spending ≠ automatically foreign claims; compare compatible units.

beats.say: कड़ी जोड़ो: trade की जरूरत बढ़ी, Dollar claims बढ़े, gold उतना नहीं बढ़ा, conversion पर भरोसा घटा। यही liquidity और confidence का टकराव था।
beats.on_screen: Trade need ↑ → claims ↑ → gold pressure ↑ → confidence ↓.

beats.say: इन 3 boxes में बीच की कड़ी कौन है? यह diagram gold से Dollar और Dollar से बाकी currencies का रिश्ता दिखाता है।
beats.on_screen: Three vertically connected boxes; highlight the middle box.

beats.say: सबसे ऊपर Gold, US$35 per ounce है; यहाँ ounce का मतलब troy ounce है। नीचे का arrow US Dollar तक आता है, यानी Dollar को gold का anchor मिलता था।
beats.on_screen: Gold: US$35 per troy ounce → US Dollar.

beats.say: बीच वाला US Dollar ऊपर gold और नीचे दूसरी currencies को जोड़ता है। इसलिए उसके भरोसे में बदलाव केवल US तक सीमित नहीं रहता।
beats.on_screen: Highlight both arrows touching US Dollar.

beats.say: नीचे Pound, Rupee, Yen और Franc हैं, और भी currencies हैं। इनका सीधा जोड़ यहाँ Dollar से है, अलग gold arrow से नहीं; Rupee का नाम देखकर व्यक्तिगत gold लेने का हक मत समझना।
beats.on_screen: Other currencies: Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc, etc.

beats.say: Arrows monetary links हैं, gold की गाड़ियों का रास्ता नहीं। यह currencies बनने का क्रम भी नहीं दिखाता।
beats.on_screen: Arrows = monetary links; not shipments or creation dates.

beats.say: Diagram को याद रखो: gold, बीच में Dollar, नीचे Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc। इसी बीच की currency को trade में ज्यादा उपलब्ध कराने और gold से जोड़कर रखने का तनाव समझा था।
beats.on_screen: Gold → Dollar → other currencies; connect to liquidity–confidence tension.

beats.say: 1944 के gold anchor के बाद 1960s में दावे और gold की माँग बढ़े। अब वादा निभाने का दबाव policy के फैसले तक पहुँच गया।
beats.on_screen: 1944 anchor → 1960s pressure → decision.

beats.say: President Richard Nixon ने conversion का वादा जारी रखने के बजाय उसे खत्म किया। यह official Dollar देकर gold पाने वाले रास्ते का फैसला था।
beats.on_screen: Richard Nixon; official gold-redemption commitment.

beats.say: Turning point की तारीख थी 15 August 1971। Gold और Dollar के बीच की ऊपर वाली कड़ी टूट गई।
beats.on_screen: 15 August 1971: sever gold → Dollar link.

beats.say: Dollars खत्म नहीं हुए, न सारे जुड़े institutions बंद हुए। नया सवाल उठा: gold न मिले तो दुनिया Dollars क्यों रखेगी? इसका जवाब अब oil-payment वाले रिश्ते में खोजेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Gold conversion ends ≠ Dollar use ends; new question → oil payments.

beats.say: Timeline पकड़ो: 1944 का ढाँचा, 1960s का दबाव, 15 August 1971 को convertibility बंद। अब मुद्दा Dollar की आगे की जरूरत है।
beats.on_screen: 1944 → 1960s → 15 August 1971 → continuing-demand question.

beats.say: Oil की खेप घटे तो importer का bill क्या होगा? काल्पनिक Mumbai desk पर supply 100 से 60 barrels हो; मान लो price $1 से $4 पहुँचे, तो 10 barrels का bill $10 से $40 होगा।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: supply 100 → 60; price $1 → $4; bill $10 → $40.

beats.say: माल भेजने पर रोक embargo है। 1973 के OPEC oil embargo में, खासकर Arab exporters की रोक के दौरान, oil prices 4 गुना हुए; जरूरत बनी रही, supply घटने से कीमत पर दबाव पड़ा।
beats.on_screen: 1973: embargo → oil price ×4; hypothetical arithmetic is not historical data.

beats.say: 4 गुना का मतलब 300% increase है, 400% increase नहीं। हमारे example में 100 से 60 barrels होना अपने-आप ठीक $4 price तय नहीं करता।
Oil बेचकर आए Dollars कहाँ जाएँ? काल्पनिक Saudi seller को $100 मिलें; वह नए US Treasury issue में $60 लगाए और $40 रखे, तो उसके पास $60 का debt asset और Treasury को $60 borrowing मिलेगी।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: receipts $100 → cash $40 + Treasury asset $60; government proceeds $60.

beats.say: यह oil receipts का financial assets में लौटना है। 1974 के समझौते में Saudi Arabia ने oil US dollars में price करना और revenues का बड़ा हिस्सा US Treasury securities तथा American financial markets में लगाना माना; हमारा 60/40 बँटवारा तय historical हिस्सा नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Saudi commitments: Dollar pricing + substantial investment of oil revenues.

beats.say: बदले में US ने क्या देना माना? Military protection, weapons supply और Saudi monarchy को security guarantees, यानी खतरे में सुरक्षा की मदद का भरोसा; यह रिश्ता एकतरफा financial concession नहीं था।
beats.on_screen: US commitments: protection, weapons, security guarantees.

beats.say: 1974 का अहम मोड़ था oil pricing और investment को security वाले रिश्ते से जोड़ना। Buyer का Dollar payment और seller का बाद का investment, 2 अलग flows हैं।
beats.on_screen: Payment flow ≠ investment flow; financial commitments ↔ security commitments.

beats.say: Treasury securities US सरकार के debt assets हैं। नया issue खरीदने पर सरकार को funds मिलते हैं; पुराने holder से खरीदें तो सीधे पैसा उस holder को जाता है।
beats.on_screen: New issue → government; secondary purchase → existing holder.

beats.say: क्रम रखो: 1973 oil shock, फिर 1974 के Saudi pricing और investment commitments, साथ में US protection और security commitments। Dollar में bill बनना और receipts invest होना अलग याद रखना।
beats.on_screen: 1973 shock → 1974 reciprocal understanding.

beats.say: Oil order बढ़े तो कौन-सी currency जुटाओगे? काल्पनिक Indian importer का order दोगुना हो, Dollar unit price वही रहे, तो bill $100 से $200 होगा और bank से $200 जुटाने होंगे।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: unchanged unit price; order ×2; invoice $100 → $200.

beats.say: यही oil-payment channel Dollar demand बनाता है। US ने समझा कि oil Dollar से जुड़ा रहे, तो gold backing खत्म होने पर भी देशों को Dollars चाहिए होंगे।
beats.on_screen: Dollar-priced oil → need for Dollar balances, without gold redemption.

beats.say: Importer export earnings, borrowing, reserves या currency exchange से Dollars पा सकता है। रास्ता अलग हो, लेकिन bill Dollar में है तो payment के लिए Dollar balance चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Earnings / borrowing / reserves / exchange → Dollars → oil payment.

beats.say: इसीलिए oil import bill और foreign-exchange जरूरत की खबरें साथ दिखती हैं। हमारे $100 से $200 example में gold conversion की कोई जरूरत नहीं पड़ी, payment की जरूरत ही काफी थी।
beats.on_screen: Payment usefulness supplies a reason to obtain Dollars.

beats.say: लेकिन oil Dollar की backing नहीं बन गया। Dollar देकर तय मात्रा में oil पाने का वादा अलग बात होती; Dollar demand होने से उसकी exchange value कभी नहीं गिरेगी, यह भी नहीं निकलता।
beats.on_screen: Dollar pricing ≠ fixed oil redemption ≠ guaranteed exchange value.

beats.say: Chain सीधी है: oil चाहिए, invoice Dollar में है, इसलिए Dollars जुटाने पड़ेंगे। Gold मिलने का वादा न हो, तब भी यह उपयोग बचता है।
beats.on_screen: Oil need → Dollar invoice → Dollar demand.

beats.say: सवाल में gold backing खत्म देखकर Dollar demand खत्म मत मानना। काल्पनिक नए oil order से payment जरूरत $0 से $100 हो सकती है; importer bank से $100 माँगेगा, क्योंकि invoice चुकाना है, gold लेना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Exam distinction: backing versus transaction demand; additional payment $0 → $100.

beats.say: पूरी कहानी में 2 जरूरतें अलग रखो: gold conversion से भरोसा और international payments में उपयोग। 1971 में पहला link टूटा; oil के Dollar bills ने दूसरे उपयोग से माँग को सहारा दिया।
beats.on_screen: Gold convertibility ends; transaction demand can continue.

replace_beats.say: Trade को ज्यादा Dollars चाहिए, लेकिन holders gold माँगें तो? Gold link टूटने के बाद Dollars क्यों चाहिए रहे?
replace_beats.on_screen: Trade-payment need versus gold-conversion confidence.

replace_beats.say: देशों की currencies कैसे जुड़ी थीं? 1944 के Bretton Woods System में gold से Dollar, उससे बाकी currencies जुड़ी थीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: 1944: gold → Dollar → other currencies.

replace_beats.say: French authority US$350 बदले तो? मान लो उसके claims US$350 से US$0 हुए और मिला gold 0 से 10 troy ounces।
replace_beats.on_screen: Hypothetical official conversion: claims US$350 → US$0; gold received 0 → 10 troy ounces.

replace_beats.say: यही fixed gold convertibility: US$35 देकर 1 troy ounce लेना। US का यह promise खासकर foreign central banks के लिए था, retail counter नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: US$35 ↔ 1 troy ounce; mainly foreign central banks, not a universal retail facility.

replace_beats.say: Machinery bill कैसे भरें? मान लो French importer bank को local payment देता है; authority reserves से US$350 देती है। Exporter पाता है; reserves US$700 से US$350 बचते हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Hypothetical; no offsetting inflows. Official reserves US$700 → US$350; exporter receives US$350.

replace_beats.say: Dollar world's reserve currency बना: यानी authorities विदेश के bills भरने लायक assets Dollar में रखती थीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Reserve currency: official assets usable for international payments.

replace_beats.say: Troy ounce gold तौलने की unit है, करीब 31.1 grams; 10 ऐसे ounces करीब 311 grams हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: 1 troy ounce ≈ 31.1 g; 10 ≈ 311 g.

replace_beats.say: US$35 historical rate है; French transactions teaching examples हैं। Diagram में बीच की जगह और trade की जरूरत Dollar का central role दिखाते हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Historical conversion rate; illustrative transaction amounts. Dollar connects gold and currencies.

replace_beats.say: Gold मिलने का भरोसा confidence देता था; बढ़ते trade को payment balances चाहिए थे। Reserve stock है, payment flow है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Credible conversion → confidence; trade → balance needs. Stock ≠ flow.

replace_beats.say: हिसाब: US$350 ÷ US$35 per troy ounce = 10 troy ounces। Gold conversion और import payment अलग transactions हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Gold received = eligible Dollar claim ÷ US$35 per troy ounce.

replace_beats.say: Claims बढ़ें, gold नहीं, तो? मान लो US buyer French machinery के US$350 देता है; banks से authority के claims US$350 से US$700 होते हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Hypothetical external payment: French official claims US$350 → US$700.

replace_beats.say: Gold 10 ounces रहे, पूरा conversion 20 माँगेगा। US$350 बदलें तो gold खत्म, US$350 claim बाकी: यही conversion pressure है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: 10 troy ounces available, 20 required; after redemption, gold 0, claims US$350.

replace_beats.say: 1960s में Vietnam War और welfare पर US खर्च भारी था। Worldwide Dollar claims के लिए gold कम पड़ा; France ने balances के बजाय gold माँगा।
replace_beats.on_screen: 1960s: spending pressures; external Dollar claims versus available gold; France seeks redemption.

replace_beats.say: Trade buffer बढ़ाना हो तो? मान लो जरूरत US$350 से US$700 हुई; export payments से holdings बढ़ीं, gold 10 ही रहा, conversion को 20 ounces चाहिए।
replace_beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: desired buffer and holdings US$350 → US$700; gold 10 → 10 troy ounces; required 10 → 20.

replace_beats.say: Economist Robert Triffin का built-in contradiction यही है: ज्यादा Dollars trade सँभालें, gold-conversion confidence घटाएँ। Supply रोकें तो trade की जरूरत अधूरी।
replace_beats.on_screen: Triffin dilemma: international liquidity versus confidence in gold redemption.

replace_beats.say: France की gold demand ने कमजोरी दिखाई; trade को Dollars देने और conversion निभाने का तनाव पहले से था।
replace_beats.on_screen: Redemption demands expose an existing structural tension.

replace_beats.say: Domestic खर्च अपने-आप foreign claim नहीं; international payments बीच की कड़ी हैं। Dollars और gold की तुलना conversion rate से करो।
replace_beats.on_screen: External payments connect spending to foreign balances; compare claims with gold required.

replace_beats.say: Chain रखो: trade बढ़ा, Dollar claims बढ़े, gold पीछे रहा, conversion का भरोसा घटा।
replace_beats.on_screen: Trade ↑ → claims ↑ → gold pressure ↑ → confidence ↓.

replace_beats.say: 3 boxes में बीच की कड़ी कौन? Diagram gold, Dollar और बाकी currencies का रिश्ता दिखाता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Show the three-box monetary hierarchy.

replace_beats.say: ऊपर Gold, US$35 per ounce है; ounce यहाँ troy ounce है। Arrow Dollar को gold से जोड़ता है।

replace_beats.say: बीच में Dollar ऊपर gold, नीचे currencies जोड़ता है; उसके भरोसे का असर US के बाहर भी पड़ता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Highlight Dollar as the bridge between the two levels.

replace_beats.on_screen: Other currencies → immediate link is Dollar, not a separate gold arrow.

replace_beats.say: Arrows monetary links हैं, gold भेजने का रास्ता या currencies बनने का क्रम नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Links, not shipments or chronology.

frame.process: Trace the gold–Dollar arrangement from 1944 to the termination of convertibility in 1971.
frame.how: Explain the original anchor, accumulating pressures and Nixon's decision.
frame.when: 1944, the 1960s and 15 August 1971, in that order.
frame.conditions: Confidence depends on the credibility of the official gold-conversion promise.
frame.atmosphere: International trade needs usable balances while official holders seek dependable backing.

frame.process: Explain the conversion rate and the Dollar's reserve-currency role.
frame.how: Build conversion arithmetic and distinguish reserve assets from payments using them.
frame.when: Under the historical gold-linked arrangement, before the 1971 break.
frame.conditions: Conversion applied mainly to foreign central banks; numerical transactions are hypothetical.
frame.atmosphere: French and US authorities settle gold claims and machinery payments through banks.

frame.process: Explain why increasing external Dollar claims strained confidence in gold redemption.
frame.how: Compare the gold needed for claims with available gold, then contrast liquidity with confidence.
frame.when: Pressures accumulated by the 1960s, before the 1971 decision.
frame.conditions: The conflict appears when external claims grow without sufficient growth in gold.
frame.atmosphere: Trade expands while official holders worry about the conversion promise.

frame.process: Read the gold–Dollar–other currencies hierarchy.
frame.how: Trace the three boxes and two arrows from top to bottom.
frame.when: Read as a relationship within the arrangement, not a chronology.
frame.conditions: Arrows indicate monetary links, not physical gold shipments or retail conversion rights.
frame.atmosphere: A three-level diagram connects a familiar Rupee to the international monetary anchor.

frame.process: Connect the 1973 oil shock with the 1974 Saudi–US understanding.
frame.how: Explain restricted supply, higher prices, Saudi financial commitments and US security commitments.
frame.when: 1973 precedes the 1974 understanding.
frame.conditions: Pricing and investment are separate commitments; illustrative allocations are not historical shares.
frame.atmosphere: Oil importers face expensive supplies while Saudi Arabia and the US exchange financial and security commitments.

frame.process: Explain continuing Dollar demand from oil-payment requirements.
frame.how: Follow an enlarged Dollar invoice through a bank into payment demand.
frame.when: After gold convertibility ends, whenever oil invoices require Dollars.
frame.conditions: Dollar pricing is neither oil redemption nor a guarantee of exchange-value stability.
frame.atmosphere: An Indian oil importer obtains foreign currency to pay a seller.

frame.process: Answer why Dollars could still be held without gold backing.
frame.how: Apply the distinction between redemption backing and transaction demand.
frame.when: After teaching the oil-payment channel.

beats.say: Trade को ज्यादा Dollars चाहिए, लेकिन holders gold माँगें तो? Gold link टूटने के बाद Dollars क्यों चाहिए रहे?
beats.on_screen: Trade-payment need versus gold-conversion confidence.

beats.say: देशों की currencies कैसे जुड़ी थीं? 1944 के Bretton Woods System में gold से Dollar, उससे बाकी currencies जुड़ी थीं।
beats.on_screen: 1944: gold → Dollar → other currencies.

beats.say: French authority US$350 बदले तो? मान लो उसके claims US$350 से US$0 हुए और मिला gold 0 से 10 troy ounces।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical official conversion: claims US$350 → US$0; gold received 0 → 10 troy ounces.

beats.say: यही fixed gold convertibility: US$35 देकर 1 troy ounce लेना। US का यह promise खासकर foreign central banks के लिए था, retail counter नहीं।
beats.on_screen: US$35 ↔ 1 troy ounce; mainly foreign central banks, not a universal retail facility.

beats.say: Machinery bill कैसे भरें? मान लो French importer bank को local payment देता है; authority reserves से US$350 देती है। Exporter पाता है; reserves US$700 से US$350 बचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical; no offsetting inflows. Official reserves US$700 → US$350; exporter receives US$350.

beats.say: Dollar world's reserve currency बना: यानी authorities विदेश के bills भरने लायक assets Dollar में रखती थीं।
beats.on_screen: Reserve currency: official assets usable for international payments.

beats.say: Troy ounce gold तौलने की unit है, करीब 31.1 grams; 10 ऐसे ounces करीब 311 grams हैं।
beats.on_screen: 1 troy ounce ≈ 31.1 g; 10 ≈ 311 g.

beats.say: US$35 historical rate है; French transactions teaching examples हैं। Diagram में बीच की जगह और trade की जरूरत Dollar का central role दिखाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Historical conversion rate; illustrative transaction amounts. Dollar connects gold and currencies.

beats.say: Gold मिलने का भरोसा confidence देता था; बढ़ते trade को payment balances चाहिए थे। Reserve stock है, payment flow है।
beats.on_screen: Credible conversion → confidence; trade → balance needs. Stock ≠ flow.

beats.say: हिसाब: US$350 ÷ US$35 per troy ounce = 10 troy ounces। Gold conversion और import payment अलग transactions हैं।
beats.on_screen: Gold received = eligible Dollar claim ÷ US$35 per troy ounce.

beats.say: Claims बढ़ें, gold नहीं, तो? मान लो US buyer French machinery के US$350 देता है; banks से authority के claims US$350 से US$700 होते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical external payment: French official claims US$350 → US$700.

beats.say: Gold 10 ounces रहे, पूरा conversion 20 माँगेगा। US$350 बदलें तो gold खत्म, US$350 claim बाकी: यही conversion pressure है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: 10 troy ounces available, 20 required; after redemption, gold 0, claims US$350.

beats.say: 1960s में Vietnam War और welfare पर US खर्च भारी था। Worldwide Dollar claims के लिए gold कम पड़ा; France ने balances के बजाय gold माँगा।
beats.on_screen: 1960s: spending pressures; external Dollar claims versus available gold; France seeks redemption.

beats.say: Trade buffer बढ़ाना हो तो? मान लो जरूरत US$350 से US$700 हुई; export payments से holdings बढ़ीं, gold 10 ही रहा, conversion को 20 ounces चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: desired buffer and holdings US$350 → US$700; gold 10 → 10 troy ounces; required 10 → 20.

beats.say: Economist Robert Triffin का built-in contradiction यही है: ज्यादा Dollars trade सँभालें, gold-conversion confidence घटाएँ। Supply रोकें तो trade की जरूरत अधूरी।
beats.on_screen: Triffin dilemma: international liquidity versus confidence in gold redemption.

beats.say: France की gold demand ने कमजोरी दिखाई; trade को Dollars देने और conversion निभाने का तनाव पहले से था।
beats.on_screen: Redemption demands expose an existing structural tension.

beats.say: Domestic खर्च अपने-आप foreign claim नहीं; international payments बीच की कड़ी हैं। Dollars और gold की तुलना conversion rate से करो।
beats.on_screen: External payments connect spending to foreign balances; compare claims with gold required.

beats.say: Chain रखो: trade बढ़ा, Dollar claims बढ़े, gold पीछे रहा, conversion का भरोसा घटा।
beats.on_screen: Trade ↑ → claims ↑ → gold pressure ↑ → confidence ↓.

beats.on_screen: Show the three-box monetary hierarchy.

beats.say: ऊपर Gold, US$35 per ounce है; ounce यहाँ troy ounce है। Arrow Dollar को gold से जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Top box: Gold, US$35 per troy ounce → US Dollar.

beats.say: बीच में Dollar ऊपर gold, नीचे currencies जोड़ता है; उसके भरोसे का असर US के बाहर भी पड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight Dollar as the bridge between the two levels.

beats.on_screen: Links, not shipments or chronology.

beats.on_screen: Close the official Dollar-to-gold redemption window.

beats.say: Turning point था 15 August 1971: gold–Dollar की ऊपर वाली कड़ी टूटी।
beats.on_screen: 15 August 1971: sever the top arrow.

beats.on_screen: Hypothetical assumptions, not 1973 data: supply 100 → 60; price $1 → $4; bill $10 → $40.

frame.process: Trace the gold–Dollar arrangement from 1944 to the termination of convertibility in 1971.
frame.how: Explain the original anchor, accumulating pressures and Nixon's decision.
frame.when: 1944, the 1960s and 15 August 1971, in that order.
frame.conditions: Confidence depends on the credibility of the official gold-conversion promise.
frame.atmosphere: International trade needs usable balances while official holders seek dependable backing.

frame.process: Explain the conversion rate and the Dollar's reserve-currency role.
frame.how: Build conversion arithmetic and distinguish reserve assets from payments using them.
frame.when: Under the historical gold-linked arrangement, before the 1971 break.
frame.conditions: Conversion applied mainly to foreign central banks; numerical transactions are hypothetical.
frame.atmosphere: French and US authorities settle gold claims and machinery payments through banks.

frame.process: Explain why increasing external Dollar claims strained confidence in gold redemption.
frame.how: Compare the gold needed for claims with available gold, then contrast liquidity with confidence.
frame.when: Pressures accumulated by the 1960s, before the 1971 decision.
frame.conditions: The conflict appears when external claims grow without sufficient growth in gold.
frame.atmosphere: Trade expands while official holders worry about the conversion promise.

frame.process: Read the gold–Dollar–other currencies hierarchy.
frame.how: Trace the three boxes and two arrows from top to bottom.
frame.when: Read as a relationship within the arrangement, not a chronology.
frame.conditions: Arrows indicate monetary links, not physical gold shipments or retail conversion rights.
frame.atmosphere: A three-level diagram connects a familiar Rupee to the international monetary anchor.

frame.process: Connect the 1973 oil shock with the 1974 Saudi–US understanding.
frame.how: Explain restricted supply, higher prices, Saudi financial commitments and US security commitments.
frame.when: 1973 precedes the 1974 understanding.
frame.conditions: Pricing and investment are separate commitments; illustrative allocations are not historical shares.
frame.atmosphere: Oil importers face expensive supplies while Saudi Arabia and the US exchange financial and security commitments.

frame.process: Explain continuing Dollar demand from oil-payment requirements.
frame.how: Follow an enlarged Dollar invoice through a bank into payment demand.
frame.when: After gold convertibility ends, whenever oil invoices require Dollars.
frame.conditions: Dollar pricing is neither oil redemption nor a guarantee of exchange-value stability.
frame.atmosphere: An Indian oil importer obtains foreign currency to pay a seller.

frame.process: Answer why Dollars could still be held without gold backing.
frame.how: Apply the distinction between redemption backing and transaction demand.
frame.when: After teaching the oil-payment channel.
frame.conditions: The invoice specifies Dollars even though gold conversion is unavailable.
frame.atmosphere: A conceptual exam question tests whether the learner confuses backing with usefulness.

beats.say: Trade को ज्यादा Dollars चाहिए, लेकिन holders gold माँगें तो? Gold link टूटने के बाद Dollars क्यों चाहिए रहे?
beats.on_screen: Trade-payment need versus gold-conversion confidence.

beats.say: देशों की currencies कैसे जुड़ी थीं? 1944 के Bretton Woods System में gold से Dollar, उससे बाकी currencies जुड़ी थीं।
beats.on_screen: 1944: gold → Dollar → other currencies.

beats.say: French authority US$350 बदले तो? मान लो उसके claims US$350 से US$0 हुए और मिला gold 0 से 10 troy ounces।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical official conversion: claims US$350 → US$0; gold received 0 → 10 troy ounces.

beats.say: यही fixed gold convertibility है: यानी US$35 का दावा देकर 1 troy ounce gold लेना। यह मुख्यतः foreign central banks का रास्ता था, आम ग्राहक का gold counter नहीं।
beats.on_screen: US$35 ↔ 1 troy ounce; mainly foreign central banks, not a retail entitlement.

beats.say: Machinery bill कैसे भरें? मान लो French importer bank को local payment देता है; authority reserves से US$350 देती है। Exporter पाता है; reserves US$700 से US$350 बचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical; no offsetting inflows. Official reserves US$700 → US$350; exporter receives US$350.

beats.say: Dollar world's reserve currency बना: यानी authorities विदेश के bills भरने लायक assets Dollar में रखती थीं।
beats.on_screen: Reserve currency: official assets usable for international payments.

beats.say: Troy ounce gold तौलने की unit है, करीब 31.1 grams; 10 ऐसे ounces करीब 311 grams हैं।
beats.on_screen: 1 troy ounce ≈ 31.1 g; 10 ≈ 311 g.

beats.say: US$35 historical rate है; French transactions teaching examples हैं। Diagram में बीच की जगह और trade की जरूरत Dollar का central role दिखाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Historical conversion rate; illustrative transaction amounts. Dollar connects gold and currencies.

beats.say: Gold मिलने का भरोसा confidence देता था; बढ़ते trade को payment balances चाहिए थे। Reserve stock है, payment flow है।
beats.on_screen: Credible conversion → confidence; trade → balance needs. Stock ≠ flow.

beats.say: US$350 को US$35 per troy ounce से बाँटें तो 10 troy ounces मिलते हैं। Import payment में gold नहीं मिलता।
beats.on_screen: Gold received = eligible Dollar claim ÷ US$35 per troy ounce.

beats.say: Claims बढ़ें, gold नहीं, तो? मान लो US buyer French machinery के US$350 देता है; banks से authority के claims US$350 से US$700 होते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical external payment: French official claims US$350 → US$700.

beats.say: Gold 10 ounces रहे, पूरा conversion 20 माँगेगा। US$350 बदलें तो gold खत्म, US$350 claim बाकी: यही conversion pressure है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: 10 troy ounces available, 20 required; after redemption, gold 0, claims US$350.

beats.say: 1960s में Vietnam War और welfare programs पर भारी US खर्च हुआ। बाहर जमा Dollars का पूरा conversion करने लायक gold नहीं था; France ने gold माँगा, यानी दावा भुनाकर gold बाहर निकालना चाहा।
beats.on_screen: 1960s: spending pressures; external claims strain available gold; France seeks redemption.

beats.say: Trade buffer बढ़ाना हो तो? मान लो जरूरत US$350 से US$700 हुई; export payments से holdings बढ़ीं, gold 10 ही रहा, conversion को 20 ounces चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: desired buffer and holdings US$350 → US$700; gold 10 → 10 troy ounces; required 10 → 20.

beats.say: Economist Robert Triffin का built-in contradiction यही है: यानी एक जरूरत पूरी करो, दूसरी कमजोर पड़े। Dollars बढ़ाओ तो payments आसान, gold मिलने का भरोसा कमजोर; रोक दो तो trade के पैसे कम।
beats.on_screen: Triffin dilemma: supplying payment balances versus confidence in gold redemption.

beats.say: France ने कमजोरी पैदा नहीं की, उजागर की: जैसे जमा दावे भुनाने पर पता चले कि पीछे रखा gold कम है।
beats.on_screen: Redemption reveals the pre-existing mismatch between claims and gold.

beats.say: Domestic खर्च अपने-आप foreign claim नहीं; international payments बीच की कड़ी हैं। Dollars और gold की तुलना conversion rate से करो।
beats.on_screen: External payments connect spending to foreign balances; compare claims with gold required.

beats.say: Trade बढ़ा, claims बढ़े; gold पीछे रहा तो conversion का भरोसा घटा।
beats.on_screen: Trade ↑ → claims ↑ → gold pressure ↑ → confidence ↓.

beats.say: 3 boxes में बीच की कड़ी कौन? Diagram gold, Dollar और बाकी currencies का रिश्ता दिखाता है।
beats.on_screen: Show the three-box monetary hierarchy.

beats.say: ऊपर Gold, US$35 per ounce है; ounce यहाँ troy ounce है। Arrow Dollar को gold से जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Top box: Gold, US$35 per troy ounce → US Dollar.

beats.say: बीच में Dollar ऊपर gold, नीचे currencies जोड़ता है; उसके भरोसे का असर US के बाहर भी पड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight Dollar as the bridge between the two levels.

beats.say: नीचे Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc जैसे पैसे Dollar से जुड़े हैं। यानी अपना Rupee दिखना, अपने bank से US gold मिलने का हक नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Other currencies → immediate link is Dollar, not a separate gold arrow.

beats.say: Arrows monetary links हैं, gold भेजने का रास्ता या currencies बनने का क्रम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Links, not shipments or chronology.

beats.say: Gold → Dollar → Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc का जोड़ याद रखो।
beats.on_screen: Complete labelled three-level diagram.

beats.say: 1944 के anchor पर 1960s में claims और gold demands बढ़े; conversion निभाना मुश्किल हुआ।
beats.on_screen: 1944 arrangement → 1960s pressure → policy decision.

beats.say: President Richard Nixon ने official gold conversion बंद किया, यानी Dollar claim देकर gold निकालने वाला रास्ता बंद।
beats.on_screen: Close the official Dollar-to-gold redemption window.

beats.say: Turning point था 15 August 1971: gold–Dollar की ऊपर वाली कड़ी टूटी।
beats.on_screen: 15 August 1971: sever the top arrow.

beats.say: Dollars या सारे institutions खत्म नहीं हुए। अब सवाल उठा: gold न मिले तो Dollars क्यों रखें? Conversion बंद होने से अकेले इसका जवाब नहीं मिलता; आगे oil का payment समझना होगा।
beats.on_screen: The transition raises, but does not yet answer, the continuing-demand question. Next: oil payments.

beats.say: 1944 में ढाँचा बना; 1960s में दबाव बढ़ा; 1971 में conversion बंद हुआ।
Oil supply घटे तो? Mumbai का example लो: barrels 100 से 60; मान लो price $1 से $4, तो 10 barrels का bill $10 से $40।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical assumptions, not 1973 data: supply 100 → 60; price $1 → $4; bill $10 → $40.

beats.say: बेचने-भेजने पर रोक embargo है। 1973 के OPEC oil embargo में prices 4 गुना हुए; Arab exporters की रोक से supply घटी, fuel चाहिए रहा।
beats.on_screen: 1973 oil embargo: restricted supply, continuing fuel needs, prices ×4.

beats.say: 4 गुना यानी 300% increase, 400% नहीं। Supply घटने से ठीक 4 गुना price होना कोई formula नहीं।
Oil के Dollars कहाँ जाएँ? मान लो Saudi seller $100 पाए, नए Treasury issue में $60 लगाए, $40 रखे; सरकार $60 उधार पाए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: receipts $100 → cash $40 + Treasury debt asset $60; government borrowing $60.

beats.say: यह receipts का investment है। 1974 में Saudi Arabia ने Dollar oil-pricing और revenues का बड़ा हिस्सा US Treasury securities तथा American financial markets में लगाना माना; 60/40 सिर्फ example है।
beats.on_screen: Separate Dollar pricing from subsequent investment; no historical 60/40 share claimed.

beats.say: बदले में US ने क्या माना? Military protection, weapons और Saudi monarchy को security guarantees, यानी खतरे में मदद का भरोसा।
beats.on_screen: US side: military protection, weapons supply, security guarantees.

beats.say: 1974 का मोड़ financial commitments के बदले security commitments था; payment और investment अलग रहे।
beats.on_screen: Financial commitments ↔ security commitments; payment ≠ investment.

beats.say: Treasury securities सरकार के उधार की receipt जैसी हैं। नया issue सरकार को पैसा देता है; पुराना खरीदो तो seller को।
beats.on_screen: New issue → government borrowing; secondary purchase → existing holder.

beats.say: 1973 में oil shock आया; 1974 में Saudi financial और US security commitments जुड़े।
beats.on_screen: 1973 shock → 1974 reciprocal commitments.

beats.say: Order दोगुना हो तो? Indian importer का example लो: unit price वही, oil bill $100 से $200; bank से $200 जुटाने होंगे।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: order ×2; unchanged Dollar unit price; invoice $100 → $200.

beats.say: यही oil-payment channel है: US ने समझा, Dollar में oil bills हों तो gold backing बिना भी Dollars चाहिए होंगे।
beats.on_screen: Dollar-priced oil → Dollar payment needs, independent of gold conversion.

beats.say: Dollars export earnings, borrowing, reserves या exchange से मिलें; invoice चुकाने के लिए उनका balance चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Obtain Dollars → settle Dollar invoice.

beats.say: Oil-import news में यही जरूरत मिलती है: bill भरना है, gold लेना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Oil bills create foreign-exchange needs.

beats.say: Oil pricing backing नहीं: Dollar देकर fixed oil मिलने का promise नहीं। Demand से exchange value कभी न गिरने की guarantee भी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Dollar pricing ≠ oil redemption ≠ guaranteed exchange value.

beats.say: Oil चाहिए, invoice Dollars में है, इसलिए Dollars चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Oil need → Dollar invoice → Dollar demand.

beats.say: Exam में backing और use अलग रखो। मान लो नया oil bill payment जरूरत $0 से $100 करे; bank से Dollars माँगना gold बिना भी समझ आता है।
beats.on_screen: Conceptual exam question: loss of gold backing does not eliminate transaction demand.

beats.say: Gold conversion खत्म होना, payment में Dollar की जरूरत खत्म होना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Gold redemption ≠ transaction demand.

output.title: Gold link टूटा, फिर भी Dollar की माँग क्यों रही?

frame.process: Trace the gold–Dollar arrangement from 1944 to the termination of convertibility in 1971.
frame.how: Explain the original anchor, accumulating pressures and Nixon's decision.
frame.when: 1944, the 1960s and 15 August 1971, in that order.
frame.conditions: Confidence depends on the credibility of the official gold-conversion promise.
frame.atmosphere: International trade needs usable balances while official holders seek dependable backing.

frame.process: Explain the conversion rate and the Dollar's reserve-currency role.
frame.how: Build conversion arithmetic and distinguish reserve assets from payments using them.
frame.when: Under the historical gold-linked arrangement, before the 1971 break.
frame.conditions: Conversion applied mainly to foreign central banks; numerical transactions are hypothetical.
frame.atmosphere: French and US authorities settle gold claims and machinery payments through banks.

frame.process: Explain why increasing external Dollar claims strained confidence in gold redemption.
frame.how: Compare the gold needed for claims with available gold, then contrast liquidity with confidence.
frame.when: Pressures accumulated by the 1960s, before the 1971 decision.
frame.conditions: The conflict appears when external claims grow without sufficient growth in gold.
frame.atmosphere: Trade expands while official holders worry about the conversion promise.

frame.process: Read the gold–Dollar–other currencies hierarchy.
frame.how: Trace the three boxes and two arrows from top to bottom.
frame.when: Read as a relationship within the arrangement, not a chronology.
frame.conditions: Arrows indicate monetary links, not physical gold shipments or retail conversion rights.
frame.atmosphere: A three-level diagram connects a familiar Rupee to the international monetary anchor.

frame.process: Connect the 1973 oil shock with the 1974 Saudi–US understanding.
frame.how: Explain restricted supply, higher prices, Saudi financial commitments and US security commitments.
frame.when: 1973 precedes the 1974 understanding.
frame.conditions: Pricing and investment are separate commitments; illustrative allocations are not historical shares.
frame.atmosphere: Oil importers face expensive supplies while Saudi Arabia and the US exchange financial and security commitments.

frame.process: Explain continuing Dollar demand from oil-payment requirements.
frame.how: Follow an enlarged Dollar invoice through a bank into payment demand.
frame.when: After gold convertibility ends, whenever oil invoices require Dollars.
frame.conditions: Dollar pricing is neither oil redemption nor a guarantee of exchange-value stability.
frame.atmosphere: An Indian oil importer obtains foreign currency to pay a seller.

frame.process: Answer why Dollars could still be held without gold backing.
frame.how: Apply the distinction between redemption backing and transaction demand.
frame.when: After teaching the oil-payment channel.
frame.conditions: The invoice specifies Dollars even though gold conversion is unavailable.
frame.atmosphere: A conceptual exam question tests whether the learner confuses backing with usefulness.

beats.say: Trade को ज्यादा Dollars चाहिए, लेकिन holders gold माँगें तो? Gold link टूटने के बाद Dollars क्यों चाहिए रहे?
beats.on_screen: Trade-payment need versus gold-conversion confidence.

beats.say: देशों की currencies कैसे जुड़ी थीं? 1944 के Bretton Woods System में gold से Dollar, उससे बाकी currencies जुड़ी थीं।
beats.on_screen: 1944: gold → Dollar → other currencies.

beats.say: French authority US$350 बदले तो? मान लो उसके claims US$350 से US$0 हुए और मिला gold 0 से 10 troy ounces।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical official conversion: claims US$350 → US$0; gold received 0 → 10 troy ounces.

beats.say: यही fixed gold convertibility है: यानी US$35 देकर 1 troy ounce gold लेना। वादा खासकर foreign central banks के लिए था, आम ग्राहक के लिए नहीं।
beats.on_screen: US$35 ↔ 1 troy ounce; mainly foreign central banks, not a retail entitlement.

beats.say: Machinery bill कैसे भरें? मान लो French importer bank को local payment देता है; authority reserves से US$350 देती है। Exporter पाता है; reserves US$700 से US$350 बचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical; no offsetting inflows. Official reserves US$700 → US$350; exporter receives US$350.

beats.say: Dollar world's reserve currency बना: यानी authorities विदेश के bills भरने लायक assets Dollar में रखती थीं।
beats.on_screen: Reserve currency: official assets usable for international payments.

beats.say: Troy ounce gold तौलने की unit है, करीब 31.1 grams; 10 ऐसे ounces करीब 311 grams हैं।
beats.on_screen: 1 troy ounce ≈ 31.1 g; 10 ≈ 311 g.

beats.say: US$35 historical rate है; French transactions teaching examples हैं। Diagram में बीच की जगह और trade की जरूरत Dollar का central role दिखाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Historical conversion rate; illustrative transaction amounts. Dollar connects gold and currencies.

beats.say: Gold मिलने का भरोसा confidence देता था; बढ़ते trade को payment balances चाहिए थे। Reserve stock है, payment flow है।
beats.on_screen: Credible conversion → confidence; trade → balance needs. Stock ≠ flow.

beats.say: US$350 को US$35 per troy ounce से बाँटें तो 10 troy ounces मिलते हैं। Import payment में gold नहीं मिलता।
beats.on_screen: Gold received = eligible Dollar claim ÷ US$35 per troy ounce.

beats.say: Claims बढ़ें, gold नहीं, तो? मान लो US buyer French machinery के US$350 देता है; banks से authority के claims US$350 से US$700 होते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical external payment: French official claims US$350 → US$700.

beats.say: Gold 10 ounces रहे, पूरा conversion 20 माँगेगा। US$350 बदलें तो gold खत्म, US$350 claim बाकी: यही conversion pressure है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: 10 troy ounces available, 20 required; after redemption, gold 0, claims US$350.

beats.say: 1960s में Vietnam War और welfare programs पर भारी US खर्च हुआ। बाहर के Dollars बदलने लायक gold नहीं था; France ने Dollars के बदले gold माँगा।
beats.on_screen: 1960s: spending pressures; external claims strain available gold; France seeks redemption.

beats.say: Trade buffer बढ़ाना हो तो? मान लो जरूरत US$350 से US$700 हुई; export payments से holdings बढ़ीं, gold 10 ही रहा, conversion को 20 ounces चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: desired buffer and holdings US$350 → US$700; gold 10 → 10 troy ounces; required 10 → 20.

beats.say: Economist Robert Triffin का built-in contradiction यही है: यानी एक जरूरत पूरी करो, दूसरी कमजोर पड़े। Dollars बढ़ाओ तो payments आसान, gold मिलने का भरोसा कमजोर; रोक दो तो trade के पैसे कम।
beats.on_screen: Triffin dilemma: supplying payment balances versus confidence in gold redemption.

beats.say: France ने कमजोरी बनाई नहीं, सामने लाई: दावों के बदले gold माँगा तो पीछे रखा gold कम पड़ा।
beats.on_screen: Redemption reveals the pre-existing mismatch between claims and gold.

beats.say: Domestic खर्च अपने-आप foreign claim नहीं; international payments बीच की कड़ी हैं। Dollars और gold की तुलना conversion rate से करो।
beats.on_screen: External payments connect spending to foreign balances; compare claims with gold required.

beats.say: Trade बढ़ा, claims बढ़े; gold पीछे रहा तो conversion का भरोसा घटा।
beats.on_screen: Trade ↑ → claims ↑ → gold pressure ↑ → confidence ↓.

beats.say: 3 boxes में बीच की कड़ी कौन? Diagram gold, Dollar और बाकी currencies का रिश्ता दिखाता है।
beats.on_screen: Show the three-box monetary hierarchy.

beats.say: ऊपर Gold, US$35 per ounce है; ounce यहाँ troy ounce है। Arrow Dollar को gold से जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Top box: Gold, US$35 per troy ounce → US Dollar.

beats.say: बीच में Dollar ऊपर gold, नीचे currencies जोड़ता है; उसके भरोसे का असर US के बाहर भी पड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight Dollar as the bridge between the two levels.

beats.say: नीचे Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc जैसे पैसे Dollar से जुड़े हैं। यानी अपना Rupee दिखना, अपने bank से US gold मिलने का हक नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Other currencies → immediate link is Dollar, not a separate gold arrow.

beats.say: Arrows monetary links हैं, gold भेजने का रास्ता या currencies बनने का क्रम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Links, not shipments or chronology.

beats.say: Gold → Dollar → Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc का जोड़ याद रखो।
beats.on_screen: Complete labelled three-level diagram.

beats.say: 1960s में बढ़ते claims और gold demands से 1944 का conversion वादा निभाना मुश्किल हुआ।
beats.on_screen: 1944 arrangement → 1960s pressure → policy decision.

beats.say: President Richard Nixon ने official gold conversion बंद किया, यानी Dollar claim देकर gold निकालने वाला रास्ता बंद।
beats.on_screen: Close the official Dollar-to-gold redemption window.

beats.say: Turning point था 15 August 1971: gold–Dollar की ऊपर वाली कड़ी टूटी।
beats.on_screen: 15 August 1971: sever the top arrow.

beats.say: Dollars या सारे institutions खत्म नहीं हुए। सवाल उठा: gold न मिले तो Dollars क्यों रखें? जवाब अभी बाकी है; आगे oil payments समझेंगे।
beats.on_screen: The transition raises, but does not yet answer, the continuing-demand question. Next: oil payments.

beats.say: 1944 में ढाँचा बना; 1960s में दबाव बढ़ा; 1971 में conversion बंद हुआ।
Oil supply घटे तो? Mumbai का example लो: barrels 100 से 60; मान लो price $1 से $4, तो 10 barrels का bill $10 से $40।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical assumptions, not 1973 data: supply 100 → 60; price $1 → $4; bill $10 → $40.

beats.say: बेचने-भेजने पर रोक embargo है। 1973 के OPEC oil embargo में prices 4 गुना हुए; Arab exporters की रोक से supply घटी, fuel चाहिए रहा।
beats.on_screen: 1973 oil embargo: restricted supply, continuing fuel needs, prices ×4.

beats.say: 4 गुना यानी 300% increase, 400% नहीं। Supply घटने से ठीक 4 गुना price होना कोई formula नहीं।
Oil के Dollars कहाँ जाएँ? मान लो Saudi seller $100 पाए, नए Treasury issue में $60 लगाए, $40 रखे; सरकार $60 उधार पाए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: receipts $100 → cash $40 + Treasury debt asset $60; government borrowing $60.

beats.say: यह receipts का investment है। 1974 में Saudi Arabia ने Dollar oil-pricing और revenues का बड़ा हिस्सा US Treasury securities तथा American financial markets में लगाना माना; 60/40 सिर्फ example है।
beats.on_screen: Separate Dollar pricing from subsequent investment; no historical 60/40 share claimed.

beats.say: बदले में US ने क्या माना? Military protection, weapons और Saudi monarchy को security guarantees, यानी खतरे में मदद का भरोसा।
beats.on_screen: US side: military protection, weapons supply, security guarantees.

beats.say: 1974 का मोड़ financial commitments के बदले security commitments था; payment और investment अलग रहे।
beats.on_screen: Financial commitments ↔ security commitments; payment ≠ investment.

beats.say: Treasury securities सरकार के उधार की receipt जैसी हैं। नया issue सरकार को पैसा देता है; पुराना खरीदो तो seller को।
beats.on_screen: New issue → government borrowing; secondary purchase → existing holder.

beats.say: 1973 में oil shock आया; 1974 में Saudi financial और US security commitments जुड़े।
beats.on_screen: 1973 shock → 1974 reciprocal commitments.

beats.say: Order दोगुना हो तो? Indian importer का example लो: unit price वही, oil bill $100 से $200; bank से $200 जुटाने होंगे।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: order ×2; unchanged Dollar unit price; invoice $100 → $200.

beats.say: यही oil-payment channel है: US ने समझा, Dollar में oil bills हों तो gold backing बिना भी Dollars चाहिए होंगे।
beats.on_screen: Dollar-priced oil → Dollar payment needs, independent of gold conversion.

beats.say: Dollars export earnings, borrowing, reserves या exchange से मिलें; invoice चुकाने के लिए उनका balance चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Obtain Dollars → settle Dollar invoice.

beats.say: Oil-import news में यही जरूरत मिलती है: bill भरना है, gold लेना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Oil bills create foreign-exchange needs.

beats.say: Oil pricing backing नहीं: Dollar देकर fixed oil मिलने का promise नहीं। Demand से exchange value कभी न गिरने की guarantee भी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Dollar pricing ≠ oil redemption ≠ guaranteed exchange value.

beats.say: Oil चाहिए, invoice Dollars में है, इसलिए Dollars चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Oil need → Dollar invoice → Dollar demand.

beats.say: Exam में backing और use अलग रखो। मान लो नया oil bill payment जरूरत $0 से $100 करे; bank से Dollars माँगना gold बिना भी समझ आता है।
beats.on_screen: Conceptual exam question: loss of gold backing does not eliminate transaction demand.

beats.say: Gold conversion खत्म होना, payment में Dollar की जरूरत खत्म होना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Gold redemption ≠ transaction demand.
